alerts.title: AKI likely from dehydration, not TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines note that in patients on TDF admitted to hospital, intercurrent illnesses with dehydration or sepsis may cause deterioration in renal function. Patient has severe gastroenteritis with 5 days of vomiting and diarrhoea, hypotension (90/60), tachycardia, and two affected family members, indicating infective gastroenteritis. The high urea-to-creatinine ratio (24:1) and absence of proteinuria favour pre-renal AKI from volume depletion rather than TDF nephrotoxicity. Creatinine was normal (0.9) until this acute illness. Guidelines recommend switching to ABC+3TC+DTG only when renal impairment develops due to TDF; this AKI has a clear alternative cause. Permanent TDF discontinuation may therefore be unnecessary if renal function recovers with rehydration.

evidence.recommended_action: Resuscitate with IV fluids, treat the infection, and repeat creatinine after recovery before deciding on permanent TDF discontinuation. If renal function normalises, TDF can likely continue.

alerts.title: If TDF stopped, use ABC+3TC+DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines state that when renal impairment develops due to TDF, the recommended alternative regimen is ABC + 3TC + DTG. The clinician is considering stopping TDF permanently because of the kidney injury. If renal impairment persists after the acute illness resolves and TDF attribution cannot be excluded, the guideline-directed substitution is ABC + 3TC + DTG, maintaining the DTG backbone to preserve viral suppression (current viral load <50 copies/mL).

evidence.recommended_action: If TDF is discontinued, switch to ABC + 3TC + DTG per guidelines; confirm HLA-B*5701 negative or clinically assess ABC suitability per local protocol.

alerts.title: Repeat creatinine monitoring during admission
alerts.message: Guidelines advise that in patients on TDF admitted to hospital, creatinine (eGFR) should be checked even outside routine monitoring intervals, because intercurrent illness with dehydration or sepsis may worsen renal function. The clinician's plan includes IV fluids and antibiotics but does not document repeat creatinine/eGFR testing during admission or after recovery. Serial creatinine measurement is needed to track AKI resolution and inform the TDF continuation decision.

evidence.recommended_action: Add serial creatinine/eGFR monitoring during admission and repeat after renal recovery to guide whether TDF can be safely continued.
